What was verified

These were measured on the current code, commit 31ec88a on branch claude/grateful-design-briefing-2svp4w.

Unit tests87 / 87

Double booking, holds, forged payments, PayFast signatures, reschedule, prices, hours, phone bookings, reminders, key lockout, launch checks, studio voice. Every photograph checked in all three sizes, none left unused, none turned black and white.

Browser smoke test5 journeys

27 page renders at 320, 390 and 1440px; page titles and noindex; the Back and Back to top buttons; a free and a paid booking; then the dashboard: sign in, reschedule, set a price, open hours, record a phone booking. Runs in CI.

Lighthouse (mobile)100 · 100 · 100

Accessibility, good practice and search on all seven public pages, measured on a production build with the live security headers. Speed 84–89 on simulated slow 4G (home page 88 in three repeat runs). axe: 0 serious issues.

Offline preview1.8 MB

The whole site in one HTML file. Opened from disk (file://) at desktop and phone size with no errors.

How the percentage was worked out

Each workstream's weight reflects its share of a launched, usable website. Its progress is the share of its checklist that is done and verified. Code counts only once tested, and anything that needs an outside account counts as not done. The total is the weighted sum: 22×0.95 + 14×1.00 + 12×0.75 + 15×0.35 + 10×0.65 + 10×0.96 + 10×0.97 + 7×0.78 = 80.4, shown as 80%. Earlier audits: 72%, 77%, 78%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%, 80%. The weights are a judgement; the verified facts above are measurements.

Grateful (Pty) Ltd · Website Costing · 27 September 2026 · ZAR, excl. VAT

What would a website like this cost today?

A custom studio site with bookings, payments and a dashboard. Priced at South African rates.

This is what it would cost to commission the Grateful website from scratch in Johannesburg in 2026: the same pages, booking engine, PayFast payments, email, studio dashboard, search optimisation and security hardening, built and tested to the same standard. Monthly running costs are listed separately.

Realistic budget

R320k
About 493 hours with a boutique studio at R650/h, including search optimisation and security hardening. Range R181k–R554k, depending on who builds it. R369k incl. VAT.

What it costs, by who builds it

The same 403–583 hours of work, priced at three kinds of South African supplier. The difference is mostly rate, plus how much design, project management and testing comes included.

Option A

Senior freelancer

≈ R450 / hour
R181k – R262k

Lowest cost. One person designs and builds, so it takes longer (4–6 months) and depends on that one person for support.

Option B · recommended

Boutique studio

≈ R650 / hour
R262k – R379k

A designer and developer working together, with project management. About 3–4 months. The best fit for a site of this kind.

Option C

Established agency

≈ R950 / hour
R383k – R554k

A full team, account management and formal support agreements. Fastest delivery, highest cost.

Estimated from the measured scope of this build: 12 public pages, a five-section studio dashboard, 102 source files, about 9,700 lines of code and 82 automated tests. The cost column uses the boutique-studio rate.

The services this site is built on. Three are billed in US dollars, converted here at R16.30 to the dollar (25 September 2026), so the rand amount moves with the exchange rate.

Monthly

  • Vercel Pro hosting$20 a month. The free plan is for non-commercial use only
    R326

Cheaper routes, and what they give up

A site that looks similar can cost much less. What drops away is the custom booking engine, the studio dashboard and the finish.

RouteWhat you give upBuild cost
Template site builderWix, Squarespace or similar, set up yourself or by a freelancerGeneric layouts, booking and payments limited to what the platform offers, ongoing platform feesFrom ≈ R2,000
WordPress with booking pluginsA theme, a booking plugin and a PayFast pluginPlugin-shaped booking flow and admin, weaker double-booking guarantees, more upkeep and security patchingR40k – R90k
Custom build like this oneDesigned to the CI; booking rules and dashboard made for the studioNothing. It costs more up front, but the studio owns the codeR181k – R554k

To finish this site from where it stands

This build is 80% complete. Almost all of the remaining 20% is content from the studio and opening accounts, which are not developer costs.

Developer time still needed: about 11–18 hours, R4,950 – R17,100. Setting up Supabase, PayFast, Resend and Vercel; connecting the domain; verifying Google Search Console and submitting the sitemap; a PayFast sandbox test; testing on real phones; and the changes from the studio’s review. After that, only the monthly running costs of about R744 remain, plus PayFast’s fee on each payment.

Not included in these figures

  • PhotographyAn editorial fashion shoot. Get quotes from photographers, and confirm image rights in writing
  • Logo and brand identityAlready exists in the CI manual
  • Advertising, ongoing SEO campaigns and social media managementThe on-site search optimisation is included; paid ads and monthly SEO work are not
  • VAT at 15%Added if the supplier is VAT-registered. The R320k budget becomes R369k

How this was worked out

Hours are an estimate for a competent South African team building this exact scope from scratch, measured against the finished code. Hourly rates are placed within published 2026 South African ranges: freelancers R350–R900 (senior React and Node developers R700–R1,200) and agencies R450–R1,200. Actual quotes vary by supplier and by how much scope is trimmed. Service prices and the PayFast fee are the providers’ published 2026 rates. The rand amounts for dollar-billed services use R16.30 to the dollar.
